guarantees.promise: the HTTP gateway requires a credential on every non-public route
scoped or named tokens close the gateway with a per-route scope floor
human operators authenticate to the gateway through the IdP, groups mapped to scopes
the gateway serves HTTPS, so bearers and JWTs do not cross the wire in cleartext
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[gateway_tls]` (or TLS terminated by a proxy in front — not visible here)

guarantees.promise: a provider sees the gateway's client as the caller, attested by the gateway's identity
gossip is mTLS: every peer presents a certificate signed by the fleet CA
an identity entry this node cannot authenticate is rejected (issuer binding rests on it)
the fleet CA's private key is not on this node, so a removed member cannot mint itself a new identity here
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls] cert_pem` + `key_pem` (a node certificate issued off-node: `mycelium tls issue`); no `ca-key.pem` in this node's certificate directory

guarantees.promise: every gateway dispatch is authorised by policy before it runs — permit, deny or indeterminate
every authorisation decision is journalled, fsynced, before dispatch
protected work (`mcp.invoke`, `skill.invoke`, …) is authorised where it runs, not only at a gateway
guarantees.needs: `gateway` + `tls`; `with_provider_enforcement` (with an evaluator; without one every protected call is refused)

guarantees.promise: `/a2a` is not anonymous skill dispatch
guarantees.needs: `a2a`; an evaluator that denies anonymous principals — a bearer does not gate this route

guarantees.promise: mandates are established and verified at this node (scoped authority, revocation)
a restart does not restore revoked authority: installed epochs are journalled first
governance actions at the gateway are sealed into the tamper-evident chain
guarantees.needs: `compliance`; `[tls]` (records are sealed with the node identity)

guarantees.promise: sealed records are mirrored to an external sink (SIEM / WORM), original bytes kept

the substrate's own outbound calls are restricted to a hostname allow-list (MCP bridge, LLM, probes, skillrunner, the wasm host, the wiki sink, the federation client, OIDC) — the first URL and every redirect hop, with the host read the way the client reads it
guarantees.needs: `egress.allow_hosts` non-empty (empty allows all); the federation client (the node's policy applied to clients it is handed, `FederationClient::with_egress` elsewhere) and OIDC discovery + JWKS since 2026-10-03 (a denied issuer refuses `start()`). Since 2.22.1: every redirect hop re-checked (≤ 5, never https → http), none followed by a client without the policy or carrying a credential header (`mycelium::egress_client`); the host parsed with the client's own WHATWG parser; an object store gated on the endpoint it dials, not its bucket. An `HttpLibrarySource` or `OllamaProbe` built outside an agent is gated only when built `with_egress`. **Not covered:** name resolution (an allowed name resolving to a denied address), a cloud identity's credential traffic, redirects inside `object_store`'s own client

guarantees.promise: a restart recovers the KV and acceptor memory from disk
a WAL acknowledgement is a durability claim: the write is on disk before the ack
a node does not start over persisted state it could not read — nothing is compacted over an unreadable snapshot or WAL
the WAL and snapshot are encrypted at rest
safety-sensitive agreement runs the supported profile: a fixed voter set, a strict-majority quorum, identical trust slices
guarantees.needs: chosen per proposal in `ConsensusConfig`; nothing validates it (plan §8)

guarantees.promise: agent pods reach nothing but their gateway
guarantees.needs: the network: separate pods, an enforcing CNI, a NetworkPolicy

guarantees.promise: this node's wall clock is within the bound every expiry and freshness check assumes
